diagnostic_evidence.quote: including the definition of Zipper Iterated Function Systems (ZIFS)

issues.failure_explanation: The cited rational-spline FIF theorem assumes L_i(x_1)=x_i, L_i(x_n)=x_{i+1} with a_i>0, and join-up conditions F_{i,m}(x_n,.)=F_{i+1,m}(x_1,.) between consecutive maps. The RCTZFIF uses signature-dependent maps. For eps_j=1 the map reverses orientation (a_j<0, L_j(t_1)=t_{j+1}), so the endpoint matching between neighbouring pieces depends on (eps_j, eps_{j+1}). The condition |lambda_j|<a_j needed for C^1 cannot hold when a_j<0. The paper never defines a zipper IFS (although the Introduction promises it in Section 2). It also never shows that the zipper attractor is the graph of a continuous function, or that the derivative IFS F^{(1)} has the required fixed point with phi'(t_1)=d_1 and phi'(t_n)=d_n. The theorem is therefore applied outside its hypotheses, and the well-definedness and C^1 claim of phi_eps is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: By Theorem \ref{existence_of_rationalFIF}, the fixed point of the IFS

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a zipper analogue of the existence/C^p theorem. This means defining the zipper IFS, using |a_j| in the contractivity condition, checking the endpoint/join-up conditions for the value and derivative IFS for arbitrary signatures, and showing the operator is a contraction whose fixed point is C^1.
issues.overall_effect: The central object phi_eps (existence as a continuous graph, uniqueness, C^1 smoothness) is not established for signatures with eps_j=1, which are exactly the zipper cases used in the experiments. The later theorems take phi_eps as given.
issues.title: Existence and C^1 smoothness of the zipper RCTZFIF derived from a theorem for ordinary (orientation-preserving) IFS
issues.why_classification: The standard fixed-point argument adapts to the zipper setting, but it needs a new, contained lemma with verification of the join-up conditions. No change to the construction or the results is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions
Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The self-referential equations of phi_eps and phi use different maps. phi_eps(L_{j,eps}(t)) = lambda_j phi_eps(t)+M_{j,eps}(t), whereas phi(L_j(t)) = lambda_j phi(t)+M_j(t). For eps_j=1, L_{j,eps} is the reflection of L_j inside I_j. The difference phi_eps(s)-phi(s) is therefore not lambda_j(phi_eps-phi)(t)+(M_{j,eps}-M_j)(t) at a common t. The comparison picks up terms such as lambda_j(phi(t')-phi(t)) and M_{j,eps}(t')-M_j(t) with t'=t_1+t_n-t, which are not small. The contraction step ||phi_eps-phi|| <= |lambda| ||phi_eps-phi|| + ||M_{j,eps}-M_j|| is therefore unjustified. Even taken at face value, the final bound ||eps||_inf (C*Phi + 4h eta/pi)/(1-|lambda|) with Phi = max|f_j| does not tend to 0 as h->0 whenever some eps_j=1, and the cited term |lambda|/(1-|lambda|)(E+E*) vanishes only if lambda->0. The bound therefore cannot establish the advertised convergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate with the reflection explicitly: compare phi_eps(L_{j,eps}(t)) with phi(L_j(t')) and add the oscillation terms lambda_j(phi(t')-phi(t)) and M_{j,eps}(t')-M_j(t). Replace Phi by consecutive data/derivative differences, which are O(h). State the result as an error bound that vanishes only in a regime such as h->0 together with |lambda|_inf->0 (or eps=0), and weaken the prose claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence theorem, the headline error analysis, and the abstract/conclusion claims of convergence to the classical FIF and to psi are not supported for reversed (eps_j=1) segments.
issues.title: Comparison of phi_eps with phi ignores the reversed maps; derived bound does not give convergence
issues.why_classification: The key comparison inequality fails structurally, and the corrected bound has different terms and a restricted convergence regime. The stated convergence guarantee for general signatures and scalings is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Replacing 1/|q_{j,eps}(theta)| by 1/xi is valid only if xi is a lower bound (minimum over j and theta) of |q|. xi is defined as a maximum, which reverses the inequality. The triangle inequality also cannot produce a negative coefficient in front of the d-difference norm, and a_j (hence h_j=l a_j) is negative for reversed segments. |f_{j+eps_j}-f_j| is bounded by 2*Phi, not Phi, so a factor 2 is lost. Finally, C=q/xi depends on j and theta and is not a constant. The displayed chain therefore does not prove ||M_{j,eps}-M_j|| <= ||eps||_inf (C Phi + 4h_j eta/pi).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define xi as min over j and theta of q_{j,eps}(theta) (>0). Use + signs and |a_j|. Include the factor 2, and set C = max q/xi as a genuine constant. Then redo the final constants.
issues.overall_effect: The constants and the inequality direction in the bound of Theorem thm:convergence are unjustified, independently of the reversed-map problem in ISSUE-002.
issues.title: Estimate of ||M_{j,eps}-M_j||: max used as a lower bound for |q|, negative sign from the triangle inequality, constants
issues.why_classification: Local correction of constants and inequality direction in the same chain; the structure of the estimate is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the interpolant $\phi_\epsilon$ remains strictly positive on $[t_1, t_n]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces positivity of phi_eps to lambda_j phi_eps(t) + p/q > 0 and then assumes phi_eps >= 0 on all of [t_1,t_n] to drop the first term. This is circular. A valid argument must show that the cone of positive continuous functions with the endpoint conditions is invariant under the zipper operator. One would then start from a positive initial function, iterate, pass to the uniform limit (which gives >=0), and recover strictness from p>0, q>0.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard iteration argument: take h_0 positive with the endpoint values, show by induction that T^k h_0 > 0 using the stated conditions, take the uniform limit to get phi_eps >= 0, then apply the self-referential equation with p/q > 0 to get strict positivity.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sufficient conditions are probably correct, but the proof as written does not establish positivity of the fractal interpolant.
issues.title: Positivity proof assumes the conclusion (phi_eps >= 0) it is proving
issues.why_classification: A short, routine inductive/limit argument closes the gap without changing the theorem, its hypotheses or the conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:convergence requires gamma_j >= delta_j. The experiments fix delta_j = 1 for all j, but the gamma-values for Figure 1a (and Figure 1b for j=1,3,4,5,6) are all below 1 (0.5, 0.5868, 0.5221, ...). The hypotheses of the convergence theorem are therefore violated by the stated parameter sets, contrary to the text. Either delta or the claim is misstated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the stated delta (or the gamma-values) so that gamma_j >= delta_j and beta_j >= alpha_j hold, or drop the claim that the Table parameters satisfy Theorem thm:convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical section does not illustrate the convergence theorem under its own hypotheses, and its stated parameter specification is internally inconsistent.
